messages:
maria: heads up — since ~03:10 UTC we're seeing a region-wide spike in GPU error rates in ap-southeast-1. Token-serving capacity has dropped ~18% and multiple jobs got 503s. Error stream shows rising CE and occasional Xid entries. ops-bot alerted at 03:11.

ops-bot: ALERT: gpu_error_rate(ap-southeast-1) crossed threshold (5m avg 12.3%). Incident channel opened: <https://incidents.internal/INC-2025-328>. Automatic replacement jobs queued: 48.

ajay: copying logs now. initial look — CE counts up on rack-gpua-*/node-*. nvml shows repeated "EccCorrected::single-bit" and some NVLINK timeouts. No temperature spike yet.

sam: any recent driver rolls or kernel updates in that region?

maria: no driver rolls from infra in the last 48h. We did push a probe-config change (telemetry agent v2.3.1) yesterday.

leo: I see the same in telemetry. Probe ingestion lagging; some cards flip between healthy/flaky every few minutes. Suggest we pause automated replacement for now — replacement churn could make it worse.

ajay: agree. If we let autoscaler replace 48 nodes it'll trigger cold provisioning and potentially saturate staging rack capacity. That could cascade to other zones.

sam: +1 to pause. How do we pause automated replacement?

leo: run: 
```
# pause node replacement in region
infractl region set-autoreplace ap-southeast-1 --enabled=false --reason "investigating ECC/Xid wave"
```

maria: run that now and hold manual replacements. I'll open a scoped canary to redirect low-priority jobs to eu-west1 to reduce pressure.

ops-bot: ACTION: autoreplace disabled by leo at 03:14 UTC. Reason: investigating ECC/Xid wave.

ajay: grabbing a small sample of nvml logs from affected nodes and uploading to /mnt/shares/gpu-fleet/2248/ap-southeast1/ for deeper analysis. Link: <s3://redwood-logs/gpu/ap-southeast1/2248-sample.tar.gz>

sam: quick sanity check — are we seeing any PCIe errors or just ECC and nvlink?

ajay: initial grep shows mostly CE and NVLINK timeouts, a smattering of PCIe AER correctable notices but no parity storms.

leo: Ops question: does Dedicated capacity for customers in that region get impacted? SLA route?

maria: dedicated pools are partially impacted. We already hit the internal throttling threshold for new allocations; contacting sales-eng for customer comms.

sam: suggestion — throttle low-priority batch traffic and enable prefix KV-caching more aggressively to reduce token generation pressure while we investigate. Could buy us headroom.

ajay: done. Applied temporary rate-limit rule: 
```
policyctl apply --region ap-southeast-1 --rule "rate-limit:batch-jobs=30%"
```

maria: also switching rollout to fallback model for token-heavy routes where latency tolerant.

leo: re: root cause hypotheses: 1) telemetry agent bump caused polling to spike and overloaded NVML paths; 2) subtle firmware regression with one card vendor exposing latent ECC sensitivity under current workload; or 3) power delivery/rail ripple affecting a cohort. Need more data.

ajay: ordering a targeted firmware snapshot of a few affected boards and running repro with synthetic load in lab.

sam: cost note — if we start mass replacements/provisioning we burn spare capacity credits and incur burst cloud bills. Approving replacements only if we see hardware permanence (consistent UE/ECC over 6 hours).

maria: agreed. For now: pause autoreplace, throttle batch, route low-priority to fallback region, collect nvml+dmesg, start firmware lab repro. I'll coordinate customer comms and update the incident ticket.

leo: I'll keep an eye on Telemetry and add a short eval metric to detect flip-flopping cards (CE_count delta > 10 in 5m and clears then repeats).

ops-bot: NOTE: incident updated INC-2025-328 — status: investigating. Assignees: maria, ajay, leo.

maria: thanks team — next update in 20m or sooner if we see a major change. :thumbsup:
